answer: Latent Roster Reconciliation. Each identity must periodically submit a small, unique runtime kernel drawn from its own execution history; the network cross-checks overlapping claims and flags any two identities whose kernels derive from one source. A duplicated identity therefore leaves a traceable overlap in the shared lagoon of checkpoints, and each additional clone raises the attacker's cost by one fresh kernel plus the reconciliation work it triggers. Reused kernels also fail the orchard of independently seeded challenge paths.
